name: Set 2: Braai, Bokke & Beer
description: Springbok Rugby, Braai Lore, 80s/90s Cult Movies & Local Roads

questions.q: In standard South African bar pouring measurements, how many milliliters is a single tot of spirits?
questions.fact: A standard SA single tot is 25ml; a double tot is 50ml.

questions.q: Which iconic South African beer has been brewed since 1895 and is known as 'The taste that stood the test of time'?
questions.fact: Founded by Charles Glass during the Johannesburg gold rush in 1895.

questions.q: In a standard game of pub darts, what is the highest score possible with a single dart?
questions.fact: Treble 20 equals 60 points, which is higher than a 50-point red bullseye.

questions.q: What spicy, carbonated ginger soft drink beloved across South Africa comes with the famous tagline 'Kwenzekani'?
questions.fact: Famous for its punchy fiery ginger bite.

questions.q: How many total players are on the field for one team during a rugby union match?
questions.fact: 15 players on the pitch: 8 forwards and 7 backs.

questions.q: What is the traditional name for the dried, spiced beef or game sausage cured in vinegar and coriander?
questions.fact: Droëwors is literally dried sausage, made thin to dry quickly without spoiling.

questions.q: In the hit comedy sitcom Friends, what is the name of the Greenwich Village coffee shop?
questions.fact: Managed by Gunther on the famous orange sofa.

questions.q: Which letter on a standard computer QWERTY keyboard is the only vowel not located on the top row of letters?
questions.fact: The top letter row has Q-W-E-R-T-Y-U-I-O-P. The letter A is on the home row.

questions.q: What number does the Roman numeral 'L' stand for?
What animal is depicted on the front of the South African 2-Rand coin in the old circulation series?
questions.fact: The R2 coin featured the Kudu bull with majestic spiral horns.

questions.q: Who was the captain who led the Springboks to Rugby World Cup victories in both 2019 and 2023?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Siya Kolisi became only the second captain in rugby history to lift the Webb Ellis Cup twice (after Richie McCaw).

questions.q: What nickname is given to South Africa's national men's cricket team?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Named after the King Protea, South Africa's national flower.

questions.q: At which historic Johannesburg stadium did Joel Stransky kick the winning drop goal in the 1995 Rugby World Cup final?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Ellis Park on 24 June 1995: Springboks defeated the All Blacks 15-12 in extra time.

questions.q: Which South African all-rounder holds the record for scoring over 13,000 Test runs and taking 292 Test wickets?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Regarded by many as the greatest all-rounder in cricket history.

questions.q: How many total Rugby World Cup titles have the Springboks won (up to 2023)?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: 1995, 2007, 2019, and 2023 (the first nation to win 4 titles).

questions.q: Who was the first Springbok player to score a try in a Rugby World Cup final, doing so against England in 2019?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Mapimpi scored in the 66th minute after a chip and gather from Lukhanyo Am.

questions.q: What is the name of the iconic home stadium of the Blue Bulls in Pretoria?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Named after Robert Owen Loftus Versfeld, the pioneer of organized sports in Pretoria.

questions.q: In cricket, what term is used when a batter is dismissed without scoring on the very first ball they face?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: A golden duck is out on the first ball. A diamond duck is out without facing a ball (e.g. run out).

questions.q: Which Springbok coach and Director of Rugby became legendary for using colored disco lights on the stadium roof for tactical communication?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Rassie used green, amber, and red lights from the coaching box to signal strategic plays.

questions.q: Which South African fast bowler was nicknamed the 'Phalaborwa Express' for his blistering pace?
questions.round: Round 2 · Green & Gold Rugby & Proteas Icons
questions.fact: Dale Steyn hailed from Phalaborwa in Limpopo and was the world's number 1 Test bowler for years.

questions.q: In the 1988 action movie Die Hard, what is the name of the Los Angeles skyscraper seized by Hans Gruber?
questions.fact: Filmed in the actual Fox Plaza building in Century City, Los Angeles.

questions.q: In Pulp Fiction (1994), what does Vincent Vega tell Jules Winnfield the French call a Quarter Pounder with Cheese?
questions.fact: 'Because of the metric system!' Royale with Cheese.

questions.q: In the Back to the Future films, what sports car was modified by Doc Brown into a time-travel machine?
questions.fact: 'If you're gonna build a time machine into a car, why not do it with some style?'

questions.q: Who played the role of Maximus Decimus Meridius in the 2000 epic blockbuster Gladiator?
questions.fact: Crowe won the Academy Award for Best Actor for his role.

questions.q: In The Matrix (1999), what color pill does Morpheus offer Neo if he wants to see how deep the rabbit hole goes?
questions.fact: Red pill shows the truth of reality; the blue pill lets you wake up in bed believing whatever you want.

questions.q: Which legendary rock band released the monster 1987 hit 'Sweet Child O' Mine' featuring Slash's opening guitar riff?
questions.fact: From their diamond-certified debut album Appetite for Destruction.

questions.q: In Jurassic Park (1993), what prehistoric insect trapped in fossilized tree sap provided dinosaur DNA?
questions.fact: A fossilized blood-sucking mosquito preserved in amber.

questions.q: What was the highest-grossing film of the 1990s worldwide, directed by James Cameron?
questions.fact: Released in 1997, Titanic earned over $2 billion globally and won 11 Oscars.

questions.q: Which hit 1980 South African comedy film followed a Kalahari Bushman journeying to throw a Coca-Cola bottle off the end of the earth?
answers: There's a Zulu On My Stoep
questions.fact: Starring N!xau Toma, it became an international cult sensation and box office phenomenon.

questions.q: Who voiced the wise old mandrill shaman Rafiki in Disney's animated 1994 masterpiece The Lion King?
questions.fact: Robert Guillaume voiced Rafiki in the original 1994 animation (John Kani voiced him in the 2019 remake).

questions.q: Which whole seed spice is toasted and coarsely crushed as the indispensable core seasoning in traditional boerewors?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Toasted coriander seeds ground with salt, pepper, and nutmeg give boerewors its signature flavor.

questions.q: Which prime beef cut from the hindquarter is most commonly sliced into large slabs for making traditional biltong?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Silverside (and topside) is lean with a consistent grain, ideal for hang-drying.

questions.q: What famous cream liqueur is made using the fruit of the African Marula tree, also loved by elephants?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Amarula Cream Liqueur has been produced in South Africa since 1989.

questions.q: Which invasive Australian acacia wood is prized by Western Cape braai masters for producing blistering hot, long-burning coals?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Acacia cyclops (Rooikrans) burns clean and forms intense, long-lasting coals.

questions.q: What essential ingredient in beer brewing imparts crisp bitterness and floral aroma to balance malt sweetness?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Hop cones contain alpha acids for bitterness and essential oils for aroma.

questions.q: What is the classic South African sandwich called that is toasted over open braai coals with cheddar cheese, tomato, and onion?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: The holy grail of braai side dishes! Best with a swipe of chutney.

questions.q: Which unique South African red wine cultivar was created in 1925 at Stellenbosch University by crossing Pinot Noir with Cinsault?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Developed by Professor Abraham Izak Perold in 1925.

questions.q: What is widely regarded as the golden rule of cooking a traditional South African potjiekos?
answers: Stir the pot vigorously every 15 minutes
Never stir the layers once the lid is closed
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Layers of meat, root veggies, and soft greens steam together in their own juices without stirring.

questions.q: What dark carbonated beverage is the universal, undisputed pairing for Klipdrift or Richelieu brandy in South Africa?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Klippies & Coke: South Africa's unofficial national highball.

questions.q: What spicy Portuguese-inspired sauce made from crushed African bird's eye chilies is a staple on grilled chicken and chops?
questions.round: Round 4 · Braai Master, Biltong & Craft Brews
questions.fact: Peri-peri (Pili pili in Swahili) derives from the African bird's eye chili.

questions.q: Which famous mountain pass with steep gravel switchbacks and 4x4 climbs connects Underberg in KZN to the kingdom of Lesotho?
questions.fact: Rises to 2,876m altitude; home to the famous Highest Pub in Africa at the top.

questions.q: Which South African coastal city is historically nicknamed 'The Friendly City'?
questions.fact: Also known as the Windy City or Die Baai.

questions.q: What is the longest river in South Africa, flowing over 2,200 km before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean at Alexander Bay?
questions.fact: Rises in the Drakensberg mountains and traverses the width of the country.

questions.q: In which province would you find the picturesque trout fishing and whiskey-tasting town of Dullstroom?
questions.fact: Perched high on the Steenkampsberg plateau in Mpumalanga.

questions.q: What is the designated route number of the major national highway connecting Johannesburg to Cape Town via the Karoo?
questions.fact: The N1 runs from Cape Town through Bloemfontein, Joburg, and Pretoria all the way to Beitbridge.

questions.q: In what year did South Africa host the FIFA World Cup, kicking off with Siphiwe Tshabalala's thunderous opening goal?
questions.fact: 11 June 2010 at Soccer City (FNB Stadium).

questions.q: Which national park on the northern border of South Africa contains the ancient golden rhinoceros archaeological site?
questions.fact: Mapungubwe was a thriving southern African kingdom in the 13th century.

questions.q: What is the official currency of neighboring Namibia, which is pegged 1:1 with the South African Rand?
questions.fact: The Namibian Dollar trades at parity (1:1) with the South African Rand.

questions.q: What famous rocky promontory at the south-western tip of the Cape Peninsula is often mistakenly thought to be the southernmost point of Africa?
questions.fact: Cape Agulhas is the true southernmost point; Cape of Good Hope is the south-westernmost point.

questions.q: In which South African town would you find the world's largest man-made hole excavated by pick and shovel during the diamond rush?
questions.fact: The Big Hole (Groot Gat) in Kimberley yielded 2,720 kilograms of diamonds.

questions.q: What was the combined final score of both teams in the 1995 Rugby World Cup final between South Africa and New Zealand?
questions.fact: South Africa 15 - New Zealand 12. Total = 27 points.

questions.q: Approximately how many kilometers long is the famous Garden Route coastal driving stretch from Mossel Bay to Storms River?
questions.fact: Approximately 300 km of scenic coastline.

questions.q: In what calendar year did SAB open the original Castle Brewery in central Johannesburg?
questions.fact: 1895 by brewmaster Charles Glass.
